learning_outcomes.text: Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being capable of integrating them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics.
Knowledge about the fundamentals of electronics.

syllabus_topics: Characterization of periodic signals. Frequency spectrum.
Mathematical, numerical and hypothesis-based (trial and error) methods
Characteristic curves and DC operation models
Characteristic curves and DC operation models
Characteristic curves and DC operation models
Use of measuring instruments and application in passive circuits
Analysis of diode behavior in circuits
Analysis of transistor behavior in circuits

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of topics 1, 2, and 3 (Control Exam or Global Exam Part 2, best score taken)
Evaluation of topics 4 and 5 (Global Exam Part 1)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 10% from laboratory practices, 45% from the best score between the Control Exam and Global Exam Part 2 (covering topics 1, 2, and 3), and 45% from Global Exam Part 1 (covering topics 4 and 5). All laboratory practices are mandatory; failure to complete them limits the maximum final grade to 4.5. For the extraordinary call, the final grade is 90% from a comprehensive extraordinary written exam and 10% from laboratory practices (either previous score or a new practical exam). A final grade equal to or less than 4.9 means the course is not passed, with grades rounded up to the nearest tenth.
